steps.tx: **Anti-glomerular basement membrane disease** or Goodpasture disease is a severe autoimmune small vessel vasculitis caused by pathogenic autoantibodies directed against the **non-collagenous 1 domain of the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen**. Autoantibodies attack basement membranes of renal glomeruli and pulmonary alveoli.
steps.say: Anti-GBM disease is caused by autoantibodies targeting the alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen. Autoantibodies damage the glomerular and alveolar basement membranes.

vis.alt: Pathogenic autoantibody targeting of alpha-3 type IV collagen in anti-GBM disease
vis.caption: Autoantibodies target the NC1 domain of alpha-3 type IV collagen in glomerular and alveolar membranes. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The clinical presentation is dominated by acute **rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis** in nearly 90 percent of patients. In 40 to 60 percent of individuals, concomitant alveolar capillaritis causes **diffuse alveolar hemorrhage**, constituting classic **Goodpasture syndrome** presenting with hemoptysis, dyspnea, and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates.
steps.say: Patients present with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and alveolar hemorrhage. The combination of nephritis and pulmonary hemorrhage defines Goodpasture syndrome.

nodes.label: Circulating anti-GBM autoantibodies bind alveolar and glomerular capillaries
Complement activation and intense neutrophilic capillaritis
Pulmonary-renal syndrome with hemoptysis and rapidly progressive renal failure

steps.tx: The diagnostic gold standard is direct immunofluorescence on renal biopsy, demonstrating **bright linear ribbon-like IgG staining** along the entire glomerular capillary basement membrane, occasionally accompanied by linear **C3 deposition**. This pathognomonic linear pattern contrasts sharply with granular immune complex deposits or pauci-immune vasculitis.
steps.say: Direct immunofluorescence demonstrates bright linear ribbon-like IgG deposition along glomerular capillaries. This linear pattern is pathognomonic for anti-GBM disease.

vis.alt: Direct immunofluorescence demonstrating pathognomonic linear IgG staining along GBM
vis.caption: Pathognomonic linear IgG immunofluorescence along glomerular capillary walls in anti-GBM disease. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Genetic susceptibility exhibits an extraordinary association with **HLA-DRB1*15:01**, which confers an odds ratio exceeding **8 to 10** for developing anti-GBM disease. In contrast, HLA-DRB1*01 and HLA-DRB1*07 provide strong dominant negative protection against developing autoreactive anti-alpha3(IV)NC1 antibodies.
steps.say: Genetic susceptibility is strongly linked to HLA-DRB1*15:01, conferring an odds ratio over 8. Conversely, HLA-DRB1*01 and DRB1*07 alleles confer protection.

rows: Presents alpha-3(IV)NC1 epitopes to autoreactive CD4+ T cells
Promotes deletion of autoreactive T-cell clones

steps.tx: In intact pulmonary capillaries, the collagen alpha-3(IV)NC1 epitope is sequestered from circulating antibodies. Exposure to environmental toxins including **tobacco smoke inhalation**, hydrocarbon solvents, or lower respiratory infections disrupts the alveolar endothelial barrier, exposing cryptic antigens and triggering acute pulmonary hemorrhage.
steps.say: Alveolar basement membrane epitopes remain shielded until exposed by toxins. Tobacco smoke or volatile hydrocarbons disrupt endothelium to trigger pulmonary hemorrhage.

nodes.label: Cryptic alpha-3(IV)NC1 epitopes shielded by intact alveolar endothelium
Inhalation of cigarette smoke or hydrocarbons causes capillary disruption
Anti-GBM antibodies access basement membrane, triggering alveolar hemorrhage

steps.tx: Between **20 and 35 percent** of patients with anti-GBM disease exhibit concurrent **double-positive ANCA**, predominantly targeting myeloperoxidase or MPO-ANCA. Double-positive patients typically behave like ANCA-associated vasculitis with higher long-term relapse rates, requiring prolonged maintenance immunosuppression.
steps.say: Up to 35 percent of anti-GBM patients are double-positive for ANCA, mostly MPO-ANCA. Double-positive cases exhibit higher relapse rates requiring maintenance therapy.

right.title: Double-positive (anti-GBM + ANCA)
points: Relapses occur in up to 25 to 30%

steps.tx: Emergency induction combines daily **therapeutic plasma exchange** for **14 consecutive days** with high-dose oral **prednisone at 1 mg/kg daily** and **oral cyclophosphamide at 2 mg/kg daily**. Plasma exchange mechanically clears pathogenic circulating anti-GBM autoantibodies, while cyclophosphamide arrests ongoing de novo antibody production.
steps.say: Immediate treatment combines daily plasma exchange for 14 days with prednisone and cyclophosphamide. Plasma exchange clears circulating antibodies while cyclophosphamide stops synthesis.

rows: 4-liter exchange daily for 14 days or until anti-GBM undetectable
Rapidly clears circulating pathogenic IgG antibodies
IV methylprednisolone 1 g x 3 days, then oral prednisone 1 mg/kg
Suppresses acute glomerular and alveolar inflammation
Oral 2 mg/kg/day or pulsed IV for 2 to 3 months

steps.tx: Renal recovery correlates directly with serum creatinine at clinical presentation. When patients present **dialysis-dependent with 100 percent cellular crescents** on biopsy and zero urine output, renal recovery is virtually nil; aggressive immunosuppression in this setting may be withheld unless active life-threatening pulmonary hemorrhage is present.
steps.say: Dialysis dependence and 100 percent glomerular crescents at presentation portend virtually zero renal recovery. Aggressive therapy is reserved if alveolar hemorrhage coexists.

nodes.label: Serum creatinine <5.7 mg/dL at diagnosis: high renal recovery rate
Serum creatinine >5.7 mg/dL: variable recovery with urgent therapy
Oliguric dialysis-dependence with 100% crescents: virtually zero recovery
